title: CAT: Closed-loop Adversarial Training for Safe End-to-End Driving

control_signal.value: A collision objective against the learner's estimated ego trajectory (risk-conditioned Bayesian formulation); one opponent vehicle is attacked per scene. No user-specified attributes.

control_mechanism.value: Factorized resampling: draw M=32 opponent trajectory candidates from a pretrained motion predictor (DenseTNT), weight them by ego-rollout estimates and a collision likelihood with decay alpha=0.99, then select numerically.

base_model.value: Pretrained motion forecasters (DenseTNT, M2I) as traffic prior; TD3 reinforcement-learning ego policy trained in MetaDrive.

datasets.value: 500 Waymo Open Motion Dataset scenarios imported into MetaDrive; 400 train and 100 held-out test; 9 s scenes, 1 s history.

metrics.value: Route completion and crash rate on log-replay and safety-critical test scenarios; attack success and computation time compared with STRIVE and M2I.

controllability_evidence.value: Closed-loop training lowers crash rate from 19.89 % to 13.43 % (log-replay) and 43.33 % to 28.15 % (safety-critical), i.e. 6.46 and 15.18 points, with competitive route completion.

stated_limitations.value: Only adversarial vehicles (no pedestrians or cyclists); only 500 scenes, so other failure modes may remain; only RL driving policies studied, not imitation or human-in-the-loop.

notes: Primarily adversarial training of an ego policy; scenario generation is adversarial resampling, not user-steerable generation. Family label 'other' is a judgment call.
